liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **On the Road Again** (2 reviews): Performance was not tight, but the subsequent Jack-A-Roe made up for the looseness; Jerry's guitar tone edges closer to the Stranger/Shakedown sound, though not quite there [10][18]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (2 reviews): Minglewood demonstrates the rocking, energized Grateful Dead at their best during this run; Great fuzz sound is heard on Jerry's guitar during the Minglewood solo section [12][18]
- **It Must Have Been the Roses** (1 review): Listener notes the song and The Race Is On gained new life after acoustic shows [10]
- **Eyes of the World** (1 review): Jerry Garcia is on fire throughout the song, with great stuff at the end of Estimated Prophet [11]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Listener calls the rendering of Wharf Rat epic, noting interesting drums and space sections [11]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-11-26.132344.mtx.dusborne.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 180 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [1]. Said about its sound: Matrix recording is clear on headphones, revealing subtleties in the performance and tone [18]
- **gd1980-11-26.134094.sbd.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 177 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [2]. Said about its sound: Listener reiterates that good things come to those who wait for this recording [20]
- **gd1980-11-26.sbd.clugston-edited.patched.82278.shnf**: soundboard; 25 songs; 173 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: Heavy crowd presence in the AUD makes the Eyes of the World patch transition rough [3]
- **gd1980-11-26.150965.mtx.chappell.sb33a.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 25 songs; 178 min [5]
- **gd1980-11-26.beyerm160.wise.miller.101699.flac16**: source not stated; 24 songs; 179 min; rated 4.67/5 by 6 [9]. Said about its sound: Listener describes the audience recording as superb with a tremendous second set performance; Listener claims 1980-81 sound and guitar playing are essential, unlike the loathed digital era; Sound is very deep-ranging, requiring listeners to turn volume up to get the full flavor [11][14][15][16]

## Around the show

- Listener was nine years old in 1980 and doubts their parents would have allowed them to attend [19]
- SBD for the November 29 Alligator Alley show has never surfaced, affecting the volume release [5]
- The show is well played for the time, marking the first electric Satisfaction [10]
- The band was clicking in Florida after big three-set shows in September and October [12]
- Fall 1980 residencies at Warfield and RCMH had tentative electric sets, unlike the polished acoustic ones [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-11-26.132344.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Dave Usborne; source: 2 Source Matrix by Dusborne; Soundboard (shnid:03380) Source: Master Soundboard Cassette > Cassette > DAT > CDRCD and Audience (shnid:101699) Beyer M160 ->… [1]. Also: Setlist and show information are embedded in the FLAC file headers for player display [1]
- **gd1980-11-26.134094.sbd.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat [2]
- **gd1980-11-26.sbd.clugston-edited.patched.82278.shnf**: transferred by Bill Tetzeli; source: Master Soundboard Cassette > Cassette > DAT > CDR [3]. Also: Uploader patched beginnings of three songs using Jim Wise AUD, fixing SBEs with shntool [3]
- **gd1980-11-26.150965.mtx.chappell.sb33a.flac16**: transferred by Matrixed by Chris Chappell; source: Matrix (SBD/AUD mix) ratio ~ Phi (the Golden Ratio) - 1.618/1 or 62%/38% [5]. Also: Matrix was held for four years to release with other late fall shows for the 30th anniversary; Credits include Scott Clugston for SBD, Jim Wise for AUD, and Paul B and Willy [5]
- **gd1980-11-26.beyerm160.wise.miller.101699.flac16**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Beyer M160 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell UDXLII-C90/Dolby B) [9]
